what_it_does: Designing an analog circuit — one that works with continuous voltages rather than just 0s and 1s — requires choosing dozens of component sizes (transistor widths, capacitor values, etc.) to hit targets for speed, power, and noise. Each candidate design must be verified by running a detailed electrical simulation, which is slow and expensive. No single search algorithm works well across all circuit types because each has a different landscape of trade-offs. MARIO keeps a pool of different search algorithms running in parallel and continuously shifts computational budget toward whichever algorithms are performing best, using a statistical model (a Gaussian process, which is a way of estimating an unknown function from noisy samples) and techniques borrowed from financial portfolio optimization to decide how to reallocate resources.
